newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: CRICKET-INDIAN BATSMEN ENCOURAGED BY HISTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIAN BATSMEN ENCOURAGED BY HISTORY.

text.p: India are looking to Sachin Tendulkar and Navjot Sidhu to rediscover their batting touch and reawaken some bad memories for West Indies in the second test starting at Queen's Park on Friday.

The drawn first test in Jamaica was shaped by a slow, low Sabina Park pitch which gave scant help to the home side's pace attack, but ominously for the touring team neither Tendulkar nor Sidhu made a prolonged impact at the crease.

The pair contributed a match total of only 32 runs between them and the wild shot which removed the team's other senior batsman Mohammad Azharuddin for five in the Indian first innings also placed extra pressure on both the side's younger members and the lower order.
The second test in Trinidad, though, takes India back to the scene of one of their great cricketing achievements which also yielded India's last test victory on Caribbean soil.

Set 403 to win in the third test of their 1975-76 tour by Clive Lloyd's declaration, India reached 406 for four to record what is still the highest successful chasing total by a test team batting fourth.
One of Sunil Gavaskar's 34 test hundreds helped carry the day and the current Indian side will need similar resolution if they are to edge ahead in the best-of-five series.

They were bailed out in the first test by wicket-keeper Nayan Mongia and Sunil Joshi's eighth wicket stand of 67 which dragged them up to within 81 runs of West Indies first innings total of 427, and fifth day rain spared them from any further blushes.

The West Indian selectors have kept faith with the same squad, giving Jamaican pace bowler Franklyn Rose a chance to build on his debut figures of six for 100, although Trinidadian Mervyn Dillon has been called up as cover for compatriot Ian Bishop.
Bishop has a hamstring strain but is expected to take his place in a West Indian line-up which also have reason to enjoy playing at Queen's Park.
All visiting teams are aware of what happened to England, who could muster only 46 all out on the same ground three years ago, and it is also Brian Lara's cricketing home.

Lara, who scored 83 and 78 in Kingston, will be eager to reach three figures in front of his adoring Trinadadian public and his duel with Anil Kumble, who took eight wickets in the first test, could be pivotal.

West Indies - Courtney Walsh (captain), Sherwin Campbell, Stuart Williams, Shivnarine Chanderpaul, Brian Lara, Carl Hooper, Roland Holder, Jimmy Adams, Junior Murray, Ian Bishop, Curtly Ambrose, Franklyn Rose, Rawl Lewis, Mervyn Dillon.

India - V.V. Laxman, Navjot Sidhu, Sachin Tendulkar (captain), Mohammad Azharuddin, Rahul Dravid, Saurav Ganguly, Nayan Mongia, Sunil Joshi, Anil Kumble, Abey Kuruvilla, Venkatesh Prasad, Dodanarsiah Ganesh.
